# Regular Grid Traversal
## Overview
Regular [Grid Traversal](#7083-grid-based-traversal.md) accelerates [ray-scene intersection](#769-ray-primitive-intersection.md) by stepping through a uniform 3D grid of cells, skipping empty space without primitive tests [G]. It differs from hierarchical methods (e.g., [Sparse Voxel Traversal](5228-sparse-voxel-tracing.md)) by using a fixed-size array, offering high cache efficiency on GPUs for uniform data but requiring $O(N^3)$ memory [S3, Regular Grid](3950-regular-grid.md).

## Shared principles
All children use a [3D Digital Differential Analyzer](#3132-amanatides-and-woo-voxel-traversal.md) (3D-DDA) to traverse the grid [G]. The ray origin is mapped to an initial cell $(X, Y, Z)$ [G]. Distances to the next grid boundary in each axis are tracked via $tMax$ and $tDelta$. $tDelta$ is constant per axis: $tDeltaX = dx / |dir_x|$ [G]. $tMax$ is updated by adding $tDelta$ when the ray crosses a boundary [G]. The ray advances to the nearest boundary ($min(tMaxX, tMaxY, tMaxZ)$) [G].

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
class Vec3:
    def __init__(self, x, y, z): self.x, self.y, self.z = x, y, z
    def __add__(self, o): return Vec3(self.x+o.x, self.y+o.y, self.z+o.z)
    def __sub__(self, o): return Vec3(self.x-o.x, self.y-o.y, self.z-o.z)
    def __mul__(self, s): return Vec3(self.x*s, self.y*s, self.z*s)

class ObjectList:
    def __init__(self, primitive, next_node=None):
        self.primitive = primitive
        self.next = next_node

def build_regular_grid(primitives, p1, p2, N):
    grid = [None] * (N * N * N)
    dx = (p2.x - p1.x) / N
    dy = (p2.y - p1.y) / N
    dz = (p2.z - p1.z) / N
    dx_r, dy_r, dz_r = 1.0/dx, 1.0/dy, 1.0/dz

    for prim in primitives:
        bv1, bv2 = prim.aabb_min, prim.aabb_max
        x1 = int((bv1.x - p1.x) * dx_r); x2 = int((bv2.x - p1.x) * dx_r) + 1
        y1 = int((bv1.y - p1.y) * dy_r); y2 = int((bv2.y - p1.y) * dy_r) + 1
        z1 = int((bv1.z - p1.z) * dz_r); z2 = int((bv2.z - p1.z) * dz_r) + 1
        x1 = max(0, x1); x2 = min(N-1, x2)
        y1 = max(0, y1); y2 = min(N-1, y2)
        z1 = max(0, z1); z2 = min(N-1, z2)

        for x in range(x1, x2):
            for y in range(y1, y2):
                for z in range(z1, z2):
                    idx = x + y * N + z * N * N
                    c_min = Vec3(p1.x + x*dx, p1.y + y*dy, p1.z + z*dz)
                    c_max = c_min + Vec3(dx, dy, dz)
                    if (c_min.x < bv2.x and c_max.x > bv1.x and
                        c_min.y < bv2.y and c_max.y > bv1.y and
                        c_min.z < bv2.z and c_max.z > bv1.z):
                        grid[idx] = ObjectList(prim, grid[idx])
    return grid

def trace_ray(origin, direction, grid, p1, p2, N):
    dx = (p2.x - p1.x) / N
    dy = (p2.y - p1.y) / N
    dz = (p2.z - p1.z) / N
    inv_d = Vec3(1.0/abs(direction.x), 1.0/abs(direction.y), 1.0/abs(direction.z))
    
    t1 = (p1.x - origin.x) * inv_d.x; t2 = (p2.x - origin.x) * inv_d.x
    t3 = (p1.y - origin.y) * inv_d.y; t4 = (p2.y - origin.y) * inv_d.y
    t5 = (p1.z - origin.z) * inv_d.z; t6 = (p2.z - origin.z) * inv_d.z
    t_enter = max(max(min(t1,t2), min(t3,t4)), min(t5,t6))
    t_exit = min(min(max(t1,t2), max(t3,t4)), max(t5,t6))
    if t_enter > t_exit or t_exit < 0: return None
    t_entry = max(t_enter, 0.0)
    
    entry_pos = origin + direction * t_entry
    X = int((entry_pos.x - p1.x) / dx)
    Y = int((entry_pos.y - p1.y) / dy)
    Z = int((entry_pos.z - p1.z) / dz)
    X = max(0, min(N-1, X)); Y = max(0, min(N-1, Y)); Z = max(0, min(N-1, Z))
    
    t_delta_x = dx / abs(direction.x)
    t_delta_y = dy / abs(direction.y)
    t_delta_z = dz / abs(direction.z)
    step_x = 1 if direction.x > 0 else -1
    step_y = 1 if direction.y > 0 else -1
    step_z = 1 if direction.z > 0 else -1
    
    t_max_x = ((X + (1 if direction.x > 0 else 0)) * dx - entry_pos.x) / direction.x
    t_max_y = ((Y + (1 if direction.y > 0 else 0)) * dy - entry_pos.y) / direction.y
    t_max_z = ((Z + (1 if direction.z > 0 else 0)) * dz - entry_pos.z) / direction.z
    
    while 0 <= X < N and 0 <= Y < N and 0 <= Z < N:
        node = grid[X + Y * N + Z * N * N]
        while node is not None:
            hit_t = node.primitive.intersect(origin, direction)
            if hit_t is not None:
                hit_pt = origin + direction * hit_t
                c_min = Vec3(p1.x + X*dx, p1.y + Y*dy, p1.z + Z*dz)
                c_max = c_min + Vec3(dx, dy, dz)
                if c_min.x <= hit_pt.x < c_max.x and c_min.y <= hit_pt.y < c_max.y and c_min.z <= hit_pt.z < c_max.z:
                    return hit_t
                node.primitive.ray_id = origin.id
            node = node.next
            
        if t_max_x < t_max_y:
            if t_max_x < t_max_z:
                t_max_x += t_delta_x; X += step_x
            else:
                t_max_z += t_delta_z; Z += step_z
        else:
            if t_max_y < t_max_z:
                t_max_y += t_delta_y; Y += step_y
            else:
                t_max_z += t_delta_z; Z += step_z
    return None
```

## Subtopics

### [Regular Grid](3950-regular-grid.md)
A spatial [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) structure dividing an AABB into a fixed-size uniform 3D grid of cells(3950-regular-grid.md). Sets apart by partitioning space into disjoint sub-blocks where primitives can belong to multiple cells, unlike BVH which partitions primitives(3950-regular-grid.md). Choose for scenes with uniform data distribution on GPUs(3950-regular-grid.md).

### [Voxel-based Ray Tracing for GI and Specular Reflections](4091-voxel-based-ray-tracing-for-gi-and-specular-reflections.md)
A voxel-based ray tracing system using DDA through a 128³ block-occupancy grid for GI and specular reflection fallbacks(4091-voxel-based-ray-tracing-for-gi-and-specular-reflections.md). Sets apart by integrating with Light Propagation Volumes (LPV) and acting as a drop-in replacement for Screen-Space Ray Tracing(4091-voxel-based-ray-tracing-for-gi-and-specular-reflections.md). Choose when screen-space coverage is incomplete or for sky occlusion with LPV colour bleeding(4091-voxel-based-ray-tracing-for-gi-and-specular-reflections.md).

### [Optimised Voxel Ray Marching](4240-optimised-voxel-ray-marching.md)
A fixed-step [ray traversal algorithm](#7918-ray-traversal-algorithms.md) for voxel-based scenes minimizing computational overhead by keeping block lookups within the current working chunk(4240-optimised-voxel-ray-marching.md). Sets apart by replacing global coordinate arithmetic with bitwise operations for chunk indexing(4240-optimised-voxel-ray-marching.md). Choose for hierarchical voxel maps where reducing bitshifts and multiplications per step is critical(4240-optimised-voxel-ray-marching.md).

## Background
Regular grids are a foundational spatial acceleration structure in ray tracing [G]. They partition space into disjoint sub-blocks, unlike BVH which partitions primitives [S2, S3, Regular Grid](3950-regular-grid.md). Effective on GPUs due to spatial locality [S3, Regular Grid](3950-regular-grid.md).
